tagline: Old trade routes cross the plains and enter mountain country.
intro: The Salt Missions Trail crosses plains on its eastern and southern branches and mountains on its western branch. It is a New Mexico Scenic & Historic Byway. The New Mexico Tourism Department highlights old trade routes, rail beds and footpaths, along with the forested valleys of Cibola National Forest south of Tijeras. Those valleys include Tunnel Canyon and Otero Canyon.

At Tijeras Canyon, road building changed an established passage through the mountains. In 1950, Skousen, Isbell & Johnston Contracting Company won the contract for the canyon project, the first four-lane divided stretch of U.S. Route 66 built in New Mexico. Work finished in 1951; Interstate 40 now traverses the canyon along historic Route 66.

Begin in Mountainair, home to the main visitor center for Salinas Pueblo Missions National Monument. Continue through Estancia, the Torrance County seat, and Moriarty before reaching Tijeras. Tijeras marks the junction with Cedro Canyon, which leads south toward the Manzano Mountains. Follow NM 337 south through Cedro Canyon and Chilili to NM 55 east of Tajique. Farther south, Torreon occupies the eastern slopes of the Manzano Mountains on NM 55, with Manzano 6.6 miles to its south.

moments.title: Estancia
moments.text: Estancia is the seat of Torrance County. Its name appears on a 1779 map by Don Bernardo de Miera y Pacheco, marked as a town “destroyed by enemies.”

moments.title: Tijeras
moments.text: Tijeras stands where Tijeras Canyon meets Cedro Canyon, with one passage leading west toward Albuquerque and the other south toward the Manzano Mountains. Ancestral Puebloans occupied the Tijeras Pueblo site from about 1313 CE to 1425 CE. Its first phase had about 200 rooms in terraced buildings forming a U, with a large ceremonial kiva at the center. Partial abandonment after about 1360 gave way to rebuilding about 1390, but the pueblo never regained its earlier size. The village’s setting was a natural corridor between the Great Plains and Spanish settlements in the Rio Grande valley.

moments.title: Manzano
moments.text: Manzano takes its name from the Spanish word for apple tree. The Quarai ruins of Salinas Pueblo Missions National Monument lie near the town. Manzano also supplied a name to the Torreon Grant: it was named for defensive towers built at Manzano, 6.6 miles south of Torreon.
